summary: Unbalanced warmup 'samplestorm' causing sustained GPU-credit sink and autoscaler lethargy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated midday throughput degradation in their dedicated pool. Symptoms do not match a single burst — instead we see long (~10–30 minute) periods where many warmup connections from a small cohort of tenant clients cause heavy prefetching and KV-cache allocations. Internally we started calling this pattern a 'samplestorm' because many short warmup samples from the same tenant group accumulate and fail to release allocator credits quickly, pulling GPU credit balance into a low state and preventing autoscaler from attaching new slots.

Impact:
- Customer experiences sustained p50/p99 latency increases and reduced processed requests for routed batched endpoints.
- Throughput drop during windows: 25–40% on their reserved slices.
- Visible during region us-west-2 on dedicated cluster 'ded-west-03'.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ded-west-03 (reserved for SparkScribe Inc).
- Runtime: serving-runtime 2.8.1-prod, allocator 1.3.7, autoscaler v0.9.2.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer initiates a high-rate A/B test where many short-lived clients open warmup calls (length 1–5 tokens) in parallel across many connections.
2) Warmup triggers aggressive prefetcher behavior: prefetch leases and KV-cache allocations created per connection.
3) Allocator credits are consumed and not recycled fast enough because warmup samples are too short to trigger normal lease release heuristics.
4) Autoscaler observes apparent shortage of free credits/slots and throttles attach attempts; throughput degrades.

Observed behaviour:
- Prefetch rate spike: 18k prefetch ops/min at peak (normal baseline ~600/min).
- Allocator credit pool drained to 5% available for >20 minutes during windows.
- Autoscaler backoff events: attach_backoff_count increased ~+220 during impact windows.
- No driver or GPU OOMs observed. NVLink/I/O metrics show small transient increases but not at fault.

Expected behaviour:
- Short warmup traffic should not drag allocator credits for sustained periods.
- Autoscaler should be able to attach additional capacity to restore throughput within the configured cooldown window.

Attached logs & metrics (snippets):
- allocator: credit_pool.available=0.05, credit_pool.total=1600 at 2026-03-10T14:08:32Z
- autoscaler: attach_backoff=47 -> attach_backoff=267 between 14:05 and 14:30
- serving-runtime: prefetch_task.count=18321 spike at 2026-03-10T14:06:00Z
- customer request traces: many requests with only warmup payloads and immediate disconnects.

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: Customer-side warmup pattern creates many ephemeral leases that our lease-eviction heuristics treat as active, preventing credit reclaim.
- Hypothesis B: Prefetcher lacks per-connection coalescing for extremely short sessions; each spawns separate KV allocations.
- Hypothesis C: Autoscaler uses credit-based attach policy that misinterprets transient sampling as persistent scarcity and applies conservative backoff.

Partial findings:
- Heap/driver health normal; GPU memory and CUDA errors absent.
- Prefetch time distribution skewed heavily toward <10ms tasks during incident windows.
- When we manually triggered forced reclaim (debug endpoint), credits returned and autoscaler regained attach attempts; throughput recovered within ~2 minutes.

Workaround applied (temporary):
- Support applied a short-term mitigator on the dedicated slice: decreased prefetch aggressiveness and added per-tenant short-session coalescing at the proxy layer.
- Autoscaler policy temporarily loosened to allow one additional attach attempt per minute per slice.

Customer communication summary:
- Notified SparkScribe engineering and suggested they reduce parallel short-sample warmup rate as short-term relief.
- Customer accepted rolling change to client warmup sequence and will coordinate a planned test window.

Next actions / proposed remediation:
1) Engineering to add a server-side short-session coalescer that identifies many warmup-only connections from the same tenant and collapses prefetch requests into a smaller number of KV allocations. (owner: serving-runtime team)
2) Autoscaler policy review: add smoothing to treat repetitive short-lived prefetch storms as transient; avoid full backoff until credit depletion persists >10 minutes. (owner: autoscaler)
3) Improve telemetry: emit 'short-session-samplestorm' metric and per-tenant prefetch rate so we can alert before credit pool is severely depleted. (owner: observability)
4) Draft a runbook entry for Support: steps to detect samplestorm and an automated safe reclaim command. (owner: support ops)

Estimated ETA:
- Short-term mitigations already in place.
- Engineering patch for prefetch coalescer targeted for 2 weeks (2026-03-24) for canary; broader rollout after validation.

Resolution notes (ongoing):
- Current status: mitigated by proxy change and autoscaler relaxation; under active engineering work for a sustainable fix.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 — Support (Ava Martinez): Initial triage completed. Repro pattern confirmed on ded-west-03. Escalating to autoscaler and serving-runtime. Added labels and allocated SRE on-call.

2026-03-10 16:10 — SRE (Marco Liu): Looked at allocator logs; no OOMs. Found repeated short-lease hold events. Attaching debug reclaim helped recover credits. Suspect lease-age threshold too conservative for warmup churn.

2026-03-11 09:24 — Serving Runtime (Priya Nair): We can prototype per-connection coalescing at the proxy to reduce prefetch fanout. Will try an opt-in flag for the affected slice tomorrow morning and report metrics.

2026-03-11 12:40 — Customer (SparkScribe - Jason Holt): We've scheduled a reduced-warmup test tomorrow at 11:00 PT. We'll also consent to the opt-in proxy change if you can deploy it to our slice for the test window.

2026-03-11 14:05 — Support (Ravi Shah): Opt-in proxy coalescer deployed to ded-west-03 (slice ded-west-03/ss-07) in read-only mode. Observed prefetch rate drop ~65% in first 30m of the test. Autoscaler attach-backoff stabilized. Marking workaround successful for now.

2026-03-12 08:18 — Observability (Lena Kim): Added temporary grafana panel 'short-session-prefetch-rate' for the slice and a log-based alert threshold at 2k prefetch ops/min. Will hand over to on-call alarm group once validated.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary): proxy coalescer + autoscaler policy loosened. Engineering patch for sustainable server-side coalescer and autoscaler smoothing planned.
resolution_comments: 2026-03-12 17:00 — Support (Ravi Shah): Customer confirmed improved throughput during reduced-warmup test. Agreed to next-step timeline. Will track engineering RFC and schedule follow-up on 2026-03-25.
2026-03-12 17:15 — Engineering (Priya Nair): RFC created: #RFC-1189 'Short-session prefetch coalescer and autoscaler smoothing'. Targeting first canary 2026-03-24.
